nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of FeNi2O4
nodes.procedure: Typically, 0.278 g (1 mmol) FeSO4·7H2O (99%, Aladdin) and 0.582 g (2 mmol) Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (99%, Aladdin) are dissolved in 10 mL ultrapure water. Then, 2.49 g (40 mmol) urea (>99.3%, Alfa Aesar) was added into the solution under magnetic stirring for 5 min, and 0.5 mL ammonia (28%, Meryer) was further added. After stirring for another 30 min, the obtained solution was loaded in a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave with a capacity of 50 mL. The autoclave was sealed, maintained at 185 °C for 12 h, and naturally cooled to room temperature. The reddish-brown powders were collected after vacuum filtration, washed several times with water and absolute ethanol, and dried in a vacuum oven at 60 °C for 6 h.

nodes.name: FNO electrode ink preparation and coating
nodes.procedure: First, a mixture of FNO powder (5 mg), conductive carbon black (5 mg, 99%, Alfa Aesar), Nafion solution (100 μL, 5 wt%, Alfa Aesar), and isopropanol (900 μL, 99.8%, Aladdin) was sonicated for more than 1 h to generate a homogeneous ink. Then, 100 μL of the as-prepared ink was pipetted and dropped onto carbon fiber paper with a catalyst loading of 1 mg cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD reveals cubic spinel phase for both pristine FNO and V_{Fe}-FNO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder XRD analysis reveals the formation of the cubic spinel phase of both the pristine FNO and synthesized V_{Fe}-FNO deposited on the CP substrate (Figure 2a and Supporting Information Figure S2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show characteristic A_{1g}, F_{2g}, and E_g vibrational modes with metal-oxygen stretching peaks in V_{Fe}-FNO shifted positively by 3.9 cm^{-1} compared to FNO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b comparatively depicts the Raman spectra of FNO and V_{Fe}-FNO. The peaks can be assigned to the A_{1g} ... The characteristic peaks ascribed to metal–oxygen stretching in V_{Fe}-FNO show a positive shift of 3.9 cm^{-1} as compared with that of FNO.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show both FNO and V_{Fe}-FNO consist of irregularly shaped nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As visualized in the SEM/TEM images (Supporting Information Figures S2b–d and S3), both oxides consist of irregularly shaped nanoparticles with an average size of 9.6 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-HAADF images reveal V_{Fe}-FNO has abundant defects and irregular borders vs smooth pristine FNO; aberration-corrected TEM atomic-resolution images and line profiles confirm Fe vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging was performed to investigate the microstructural evolution of FNO upon electrochemical reduction etching. Different from the circular-like microstructure and smooth edges of pristine FNO, V_{Fe}-FNO has abundant defects and irregular borders ... A detailed comparison of the line profiles confirms the existence of vacancies in V_{Fe}-FNO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows similar average Fe valence lower than Fe(III); Ni K-edge shows positive shift indicating increased Ni oxidation state in V_{Fe}-FNO; EXAFS shows reduced Fe coordination number (lower Fe-O, Fe-Fe, Fe-Ni peak intensities).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Synchrotron-based XAFS studies were carried out ... These results further verify a different coordinative environment of Fe between V_{Fe}-FNO and FNO.

properties.type: Fourier Transform Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows peaks at 530.1, 531.7, 533.2 eV (lattice O, hydroxyl, adsorbed H₂O) for both; V_{Fe}-FNO shows higher hydroxyl peak ratio at 531.7 eV and F-O at 535.6 eV from Nafion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: O 1s XPS spectra were recorded ... The higher areal ratio of peaks at 531.7 eV suggests a stronger coupling between V_{Fe}-FNO and the hydroxyl species.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signal at g=2.001 with significantly higher intensity for V_{Fe}-FNO indicates higher concentration of unpaired electrons from Fe vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR test ... an EPR signal at g = 2.001 with significantly higher intensity was detected for V_{Fe}-FNO, suggesting a higher concentration of unpaired electrons.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows increased Fe content in electrolyte after etching while Ni concentration unchanged, confirming Fe dissolution creating vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP tests were carried out ... the content of Fe increases in the electrolyte while the Ni concentration experiences no apparent change.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS reveals homogeneous distribution of Fe, Ni, O with atomic ratio close to 1:2:4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping, EDS, and ICP results reveal homogeneous distribution of Fe, Ni, and O, with an atomic ratio close to 1∶2∶4 (Figure 3a insets and Supporting Information Figures S2b,S2e, and Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates (10-50 mV s^{-1}) yields C_{dl} values giving ECSA of 4.33 cm² for FNO and 92.17 cm² for V_{Fe}-FNO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the pristine FNO, V_{Fe}-FNO has a significant improvement in ECSA after the electrochemical reduction etching process (from 4.33 to 92.17 cm²), as displayed in Supporting Information Figure S12 and Table S3.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at 1.52 V vs RHE shows R_{ct} values of 453 Ω for FNO, 2.76 Ω for RuO₂, and 1.78 Ω for V_{Fe}-FNO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At an applied potential of 1.52 V versus RHE, the determined R_{ct} values were 1.78, 2.76, and 453 Ω for V_{Fe}-FNO, RuO₂, and pristine FNO, respectively.
